SUBSCRIPTION AUDIT · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

What are you actually paying for every month?

Drop in a CSV export from your bank or credit card and get every recurring charge with what it costs a month and a year, which ones went up in price, which were charged twice, which yearly renewals are coming, and where you pay for several services of the same kind. Tick the ones you would cancel to see the saving.

The file is read in this browser tab and never leaves your device; you do not connect to your bank. Independent of every bank, card issuer and service named. Figures are estimates from your file.

1. Your statement

Needs a date, a description and an amount (or debit and credit) column. Column names are matched by alias and unverified against real bank exports. Six months is the least that works well; twelve also catches yearly charges.

Choose the export file or paste it, then click Find subscriptions.

Result

Recurring charges

Tick the ones you would cancel to see what it saves. Ended charges are not counted.

Cancel?MerchantPatternAmountPer monthPer yearLast chargeNext expected

The model, and what it leaves out

  • Grouping: charges are grouped by a cleaned description: processor prefixes, store numbers, phone numbers, dates and trailing state codes are removed and the first three words kept. Two names for one merchant, or one name for two things, will be grouped wrongly.
  • Pattern: a group is recurring when at least 60% of the gaps between charges fit weekly, every two weeks, monthly, quarterly, every six months or yearly. Monthly and quarterly need three charges, six-monthly and yearly need two, weekly and two-weekly need four. Everything but monthly and quarterly must also hold a steady price (within 10%).
  • Cost: the median of the last three charges times the number of charges a year. Variable bills use their recent average and are marked not fixed.
  • Price rise: a charge at least 2% and 25 cents above the price before it. The yearly effect is the latest price minus the first price, times charges a year.
  • Ended: no charge for one and a half cycles before the last date in the file. Ended charges are listed and left out of the totals.
  • Same kind: two or more active services whose names match a built-in list of well-known streaming, storage, fitness and software brands. A guess from the name only. About 100 well-known services are recognised, so "NETFLIX.COM" and "NETFLIX INC" become one line with the service's own site shown.
  • Reconciles. The per-year figures on the rows add to the total, and the per-month total is a twelfth of it.
  • Not modelled: free trials that have not yet billed, which app is behind a charge made through the App Store, Google Play, Amazon or PayPal (those are flagged with where to look, not guessed), bundled and shared plans, taxes and currency conversion, refunds, and anything on a card or account that is not in your file.
  • Unverified: column names are matched by alias and no real bank export was available when this was written.

Common questions

How do I find every subscription I am paying for from my bank statement?

Export a few months of transactions from your bank or card as a CSV (date, description, amount), drop it here, and the tool groups charges by merchant and picks out the ones that repeat weekly, monthly, quarterly or yearly at a steady price. Each shows what it costs per month and per year. Six months or more gives the best result, and a year catches the yearly ones.

How does it decide that a charge is a subscription?

It groups charges by a cleaned-up merchant name, then checks whether the gaps between charges fit a weekly, two-weekly, monthly, quarterly, six-monthly or yearly rhythm. Weekly, two-weekly, six-monthly and yearly charges must also keep roughly the same price, so a weekly coffee habit is not called a subscription. Monthly and quarterly bills that change amount, like a phone or power bill, are listed and marked as variable.

Will it find a subscription that only charged once or twice?

Not a monthly one: it needs three charges to call a monthly pattern. A yearly charge needs two, so a file that covers more than a year is needed to catch yearly renewals. A yearly charge that appears once in your file will not be listed.

How does it spot a price increase?

Within a fixed-price subscription, a charge that is at least 2% and 25 cents above the price before it is marked as a rise, with the date and the extra yearly cost. It compares your own charges, not the merchant's published prices.

Are my bank statement and transactions uploaded?

No. The file is read in this browser tab and never leaves your device. There are no accounts, cookies or analytics vendors, and you do not connect to your bank.

Which file formats and column names does it read?

Comma, semicolon or tab separated text, including UTF-16 files, with dollar signs and thousands separators. Columns are matched by alias, for example Date, Posted Date or Transaction Date; Description, Merchant or Payee; Amount, or Debit and Credit. Some banks show purchases as negative numbers and some as positive; the tool works that out and you can override it. No real bank export was available when this was written, so tell us if yours is not read.

No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal, tax, or financial advice, and it does not replace a qualified professional. Results are estimates that depend entirely on the files you provide and the values you enter. You are responsible for reviewing and verifying its output before relying on it or cancelling anything or disputing a charge.

Not affiliated with any bank, card issuer or service. Bank, card and service names are trademarks of their owners. This tool is independent and is not sponsored, endorsed or connected to any of them in any way. Export layouts change; check yours.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record — nothing you enter is saved anywhere by this tool.

Everything runs in your browser. Your file is never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (csv_analyzed, example_loaded) are counted only in local storage on your device. The counts can be deleted with the button below. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.

Chasing card sign-up bonuses? Card Bonus Planner schedules applications around your minimum-spend deadlines and monthly spending.

Sell a subscription rather than pay for one? The SaaS price increase churn calculator tests a price rise against the customers it costs.

Free and open source. If this helped, the code is under an MIT licence — support is entirely optional and never changes what the tool does.

// Directory of well-known recurring services, matched on the cleaned merchant
// key. It does three jobs the generic grouping cannot:
//   1. merge descriptor variants of one service ("NETFLIX.COM" and
//      "NETFLIX INC") into a single line;
//   2. give the category used by the "several services of one kind" finding;
//   3. say where an account page lives so a flagged charge is one step from
//      being cancelled.
// `site` is the service's own domain, nothing deeper: deep links change and a
// stale one is worse than none. A recognised name is a guess from the bank
// text, not proof of which plan or account is being billed.
const S = (name, kind, re, site) => ({ name, kind, re, site });

// Charges whose bank text names the store or payment app, not the service.
// What the card statement shows tells you where to look, never what it is.
export const STORE_BILLERS = [
  { id: "apple", label: "Apple", re: /\bAPPLE\.COM\/BILL|\bAPPLE\.COM BILL|\bITUNES|\bAPPLE SERVICES|\bAPL\*? ?(ITUNES|APPLE)/, where: "iPhone: Settings > your name > Subscriptions. Mac: App Store > your name > Account Settings > Subscriptions." },
  { id: "google", label: "Google Play", re: /\bGOOGLE ?\*? ?(PLAY|YOUTUBE|STORAGE|SERVICES|APPS)|\bGOOGLE PLAY/, where: "Play Store > profile picture > Payments & subscriptions > Subscriptions." },
  { id: "amazon", label: "Amazon digital", re: /\bAMAZON (DIGITAL|DIGI|CHANNELS)|\bAMZN DIGITAL|\bPRIME VIDEO CHANNELS/, where: "amazon.com > Account > Memberships & Subscriptions." },
  { id: "paypal", label: "PayPal", re: /\bPAYPAL ?\*/, where: "PayPal > Settings > Payments > Manage automatic payments." },
];

export function identifyService(key) {
  const k = String(key ?? "").toUpperCase();
  for (const s of SERVICES) if (s.re.test(k)) return s;
  return null;
}

export function storeBiller(desc) {
  const d = String(desc ?? "").toUpperCase();
  for (const b of STORE_BILLERS) if (b.re.test(d)) return b;
  return null;
}
